result_text:
The Duplication report now has a "Most Frequent Duplicates" section right after "Longest Duplicates", and its code fragments are saved when `saveCodeFragments` is on. The reports module compiles and its one existing test passes, but I did not generate a report end to end to look at the page or the saved fragments.

The section method (`addMostFrequentDuplicatesList`) already existed but was never called, so the change is mostly wiring:

- **`reports/.../generators/statichtml/DuplicationReportGenerator.java`**: `addDuplicationToReport` now calls `addMostFrequentDuplicatesList` after the longest duplicates. The method already skips the section when the list is empty.
- **`reports/.../dataexporters/DataExporter.java`**:
  - Fragments are saved for `most_frequent_duplicates`, so the links resolve to `most_frequent_duplicates_<n>.<ext>`.
  - The files of the most frequent duplicates are added to the referenced-file set, as the longest duplicates already are.

Nothing is committed.

One thing I did not fix: in `DuplicationAnalyzer.addMostFrequentDuplicates` (around line 104), `Collections.sort(new ArrayList<>(duplicates), ...)` sorts a copy, so the list is never sorted. The "most frequent" entries are therefore the first N duplicates found, not the N with the most copies. This is outside the reporting change and would alter the analysis output, so I left it for you to decide. The fix is to sort `duplicates` itself.
